items.summary: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.

items.title: Bayern draw with Cologne as Kane picks up ankle injury
items.summary: England forward injured in Friday’s 1-1 draw with Cologne Club statement confirms ‘tear of ligament in left ankle’ Bayern Munich have confirmed Harry Kane will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday. Kane was substituted after 20 minutes of the Bundesliga game, having been left limping after a challenge from the Cologne defender Joël Schmied. The Ballon d’Or winner was substituted and the returning Bayern coach, Vincent Kompany, said that the injury would take “months” rather than weeks to heal.

items.title: European football: Doué carried off for PSG while Kane vows to return fresh
items.summary: Doué injury adds to that of Kvaratskhelia last month Nice 2-3 PSG; Lazio 3-0 Lecce; Gladbach 0-1 Dortmund Désiré Doué was carried off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as Paris Saint-Germain beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1. Doué went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. He looked to be in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doué to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium.

items.title: Scottish Premiership roundup: Celtic sweep St Mirren aside to strengthen grip at top
items.summary: Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan on target Hearts thrash Dundee 8-0; Frick makes winning start The recalled midfielders Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan both scored as Celtic beat St Mirren 4-1. The champions brushed off the loss of midfield pair Mika Baur and Benjamin Nygren to injury to consolidate their place at the top of the Premiership. The centre-forward Camilo Duran was also on target as Celtic killed the game late in the first half with three goals in nine minutes.

items.title: Championship roundup: Strelec sends Middlesbrough top; 10-man Stoke go second
items.summary: Boro beat Bristol City 2-0; Stoke 1-0 Birmingham Scott Parker still winless as West Ham held by Preston Middlesbrough scored a goal either side of half-time to climb to the top of the Championship with a 2-0 win that piled further pressure on the Bristol City manager Michael Skubala. Adilson Malanda’s header five minutes before half-time was followed by David Strelec’s finish in the 54th minute to secure victory. The three points were effectively secured before Middlesbrough head coach Kim Hellberg introduced the division’s top scorer, Will Lankshear, for the final 14 minutes from the bench after injury.

items.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
items.summary: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans.

items.title: ‘He wants to change lives’: the story behind Bukayo Saka’s Sócrates award
items.summary: By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue in 2022, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. He’s always asking what more we can do.” Four years on from that unexpected email, Fiesser was given the secret task of reaching out for a letter for Saka to read from the podium when he was presented with the Sócrates award at last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London for his humanitarian work.
